plan.title: Drop Node 20 from supported engines (runtime needs Node 22+)

narratives.Description: OVPR fix plan unit P2-U11 (story id ovpr-p2-u11), spec units/P2-U11-node-20-load-crash.md, issue #5873. The runtime imports `globSync` from `node:fs`, which Node 20 does not have, so it fails at load on Node 20 although `engines.node` says `>=20`. This unit sends every such import through one compatibility helper in packages/core/src/fs/glob-sync.ts and adds a non-blocking Node 20 CI job. `engines.node` stays `>=20`, as the unit spec says; the issue's request to raise it is not taken.
narratives.Overview:
The published packages declare Node >=20 support, but the runtime calls `fs.globSync`, which Node added in v22. On Node 20 the runtime fails at load. 0.127.0 and 0.129.0 behave the same, so this isn't a new regression; the stated support range is simply wrong.

**Expected:** the engines field, docs and CI matrix state the real minimum (Node 22, or whichever version the maintainers choose), and Node 20 is no longer advertised.

**Acceptance:**
- `engines.node` in the published package.json files is raised to the real minimum.
- README and install docs match it.
- The CI test matrix no longer includes Node 20, or a check fails if the engines range drops below what the code needs.

Note: confirm whether `engines` is declared in source or stamped at publish time.

Filed for @MScottAdams
narratives.StoryId: ovpr-p2-u11 (carried in the file name so the ordered plan can match it; plan.id stays the id minted from the issue, because the brief tools refuse a different plan.id)
narratives.UnitSpec: ~/Projects/directive-ovpr-planning-202611/units/P2-U11-node-20-load-crash.md (read in full; an 'Update 2026-11-17' banner wins over the text below it).
narratives.ImplementationPlan: Follow the unit spec's Fix section. Over 5 production files; split as the spec says: PR 1 = helper + five one-line import swaps + core package.json/lockfile (minimatch) + tests; PR 2 = the non-blocking Node 20 CI job (the spec names 'one workflow file'; ci.yml is the expected home) + the optional `import.meta.dirname` edits (dispatch.ts, framework-check-updates.ts, render/framework-commands.ts). If polfer prefers no new direct dependency, move the existing glob logic out of product-state-hash.ts instead of adding minimatch.
narratives.Constraint:
- Do not change `engines` in `packages/cli/package.json` or `packages/runtime/package.json` (AC16.1; D-017 O-24 keeps Node 20).
- Do not drop the Node 20 warning or change `NODE_SUPPORTED_MAJOR` (AC16.5).
- Do not make Node 20 a blocking CI gate (AC16.2 / AC15.1).
- Do not change glob semantics on Node 22+: the helper calls `fs.globSync` unchanged there.
- Do not edit decision logic in `product-state-hash.ts` or `operator-scope-limit/inventory.ts` (Scott's code); import swap only. Tell Scott.
- Do not change the host outer's failure handling here; the exit-code gap is #6201 (Phase 1).
- OVPR change gate: read ~/Projects/directive-ovpr-planning-202611/OVPR-CHANGE-GATE.md. Do not edit docs/installer-refactor-ovpr/ and do not ship behaviour that departs from the written OVPR requirements or architecture; stop that part and hand back a change proposal.
- Changelog: add the changelog.d fragment named in file_scope; never edit CHANGELOG.md.
narratives.Dependencies: Depends on: none. Blocks: none. Keep Node 20 (D-017, O-24); RC-11 not needed. The issue title and body ask to raise engines to Node 22; that prescription is rejected (AC16.1, decision row 15). The unit spec decides (D-008).
narratives.PlanningOrder: design-critique: not warranted, because the OVPR fix plan and this unit spec already decide the design (polfer decisions D-001, D-008)
narratives.UserStory: As a developer on Node 20, I want the Directive runtime to load without a module-link error, so that Directive works on every Node version its engines field says it supports.

items.title: No production source file outside `fs/glob-sync.ts` imports `globSync` by name from `node:fs`; the guard test enforces it.

narrative.Acceptance: Given the production sources, when the guard test runs, then it fails if any file outside `fs/glob-sync.ts` imports `globSync` by name from `node:fs`.

items.title: On Node 24, `globSyncCompat` returns exactly what `fs.globSync` returns for the parity fixture.

narrative.Acceptance: On Node 24, `globSyncCompat` returns exactly what `fs.globSync` returns for the parity fixture.

items.title: With the native function hidden, the fallback returns the same set as `fs.globSync` for the parity fixture.

narrative.Acceptance: With the native function hidden, the fallback returns the same set as `fs.globSync` for the parity fixture.

items.title: On Node 20 (CI job), the staged runtime's `dist/bin.js --version` and `dist/hook-bin.js` (empty payload) load without a module-link error.

narrative.Acceptance: Given Node 20 in the CI job, when the staged runtime's `dist/bin.js --version` and `dist/hook-bin.js` (empty payload) run, then both load and exit without a module-link error.
Given the change set, when the two published package.json files are read, then `engines.node` still shows `>=20` in both.

items.title: The Node 20 CI job is non-blocking.

narrative.Acceptance: Given a failure in the Node 20 CI job, when the PR's required checks are evaluated, then that job does not block the PR (the job is non-blocking).
